worklist.description: Cumulative energy transferred from a plasma-facing component into its coolant over the pulse, excluding energy retained in the component or transferred elsewhere.
worklist.documentation:
The quantity is the energy cumulatively absorbed by active coolant from a specified plasma-facing component during the accumulation interval. It represents thermal energy removed from that component, not an instantaneous transfer rate or the component's total deposited energy.

$$
E_{\mathrm{cool}}(t) = \int_{t_0}^{t} P_{\mathrm{cool}}(\tau)\,d\tau
$$

Here, $E_{\mathrm{cool}}(t)$ is the accumulated coolant-absorbed energy at evaluation time $t$; $t_0$ is the pulse start and lower limit of accumulation; $P_{\mathrm{cool}}(\tau)$ is the instantaneous thermal power extracted by the coolant from the component at integration time $\tau$. The power corresponds to the wall coolant-removal concept described by [total thermal coolant-absorbed power at the wall](name:total_thermal_coolant_absorbed_power_at_wall).

The scope is one specified plasma-facing component and its active coolant, with contributions accumulated from pulse start to the evaluation time. Only energy transferred into that coolant is included; energy retained in the component, radiated away, carried by particles, or transferred to unrelated coolant circuits is excluded.

The accumulated energy is the time integral of the corresponding coolant-absorbed power, so its time derivative equals $P_{\mathrm{cool}}(t)$ when the accumulation is continuous. It is therefore distinct from the instantaneous power quantity and from deposited energy that has not necessarily been removed by coolant.

worklist.description: Normalized count at detector pixel is the detector-pixel count divided by a positive count-equivalent reference from the same acquisition frame. It also covers count rates when numerator and reference use identical exposure normalization.
worklist.documentation:
Normalized count at detector pixel is the detector-pixel count divided by a positive count-equivalent reference from the same acquisition frame. The reference is a relative scale for that frame and must be common to the detector pixels whose normalized values are compared.

The defining ratio for detector pixel $p$ is

$$
C_\mathrm{norm}(p) = \frac{C(p)}{C_\mathrm{ref}}, \qquad C_\mathrm{ref} > 0

worklist.documentation:

$$
f_c = \frac{Q_c}{Q_{\mathrm{tot}}}
$$

where $Q_c$ is the amount of constituent $c$ in the converter material on the selected composition basis, and $Q_{\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_j Q_j$ is the corresponding total over all constituents $j$ included in the same converter material. Both $Q_c$ and $Q_{\mathrm{tot}}$ must have the same physical dimension: particle count for an atomic fraction, mass for a mass fraction, volume for a volume fraction, or amount of substance for a mole fraction.

This generic fraction does not by itself impose atom-count weighting; [atomic fraction of neutron detector converter](name:atomic_fraction_of_neutron_detector_converter) is the specialized case in which the basis is atom count. For mutually exclusive constituents that exhaust the defined converter composition domain, the fractions sum to unity and each fraction lies between zero and one; the quantity excludes surrounding detector structures and detector response quantities such as conversion efficiency.

$$

$$
